data.title: Linear and whorled nevoid hypermelanosis — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 5 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Linear and whorled nevoid hypermelanosis** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. What is linear and whorled nevoid hypermelanosis (LWNH)?**
- Sporadic mosaic disorder of pigmentation with streaks and whorls of hyperpigmentation along Blaschko's lines, appearing within the first weeks of life, progressing for 1–2 years then stabilising; no preceding inflammation or verrucous stage
- Caused by cutaneous mosaicism (chromosomal mosaicism — trisomy 7, 14, 18, 20, X-chromosome abnormalities; KITLG mutations)

**Q2. Clinical features.**
- Brown macules arranged in linear streaks and whorls along Blaschko's lines on trunk and limbs; midline demarcation; spares palms, soles, mucosa, eyes
- Usually isolated; ~20–30% have extracutaneous anomalies — CNS (intellectual disability, seizures, cerebral palsy), cardiac (septal defects), musculoskeletal (asymmetry, scoliosis) — 'pigmentary mosaicism'

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Increased basal layer pigmentation, prominent melanocytes, absence of pigment incontinence (unlike incontinentia pigmenti)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Incontinentia pigmenti stage 3 (preceded by vesicles and verrucous lesions, female, NEMO), epidermal naevus (raised, verrucous), hypomelanosis of Ito (hypopigmented whorls — the reverse pattern), linear morphoea, lichen striatus (papular, self-limited), linear LP pigmentosus, segmental café-au-lait, Goltz syndrome, X-linked reticulate pigmentary disorder, Naegeli syndrome

**Q5. Management.**
- Reassurance; examine for systemic anomalies (development, neurology, heart, skeleton); chromosomal analysis/karyotype of skin fibroblasts or blood if anomalies
- Pigmentation tends to persist (may fade slightly); camouflage; lasers ineffective in general

## Quick spotter facts
- Whorled brown streaks along Blaschko's lines from infancy without blisters — LWNH
- Hypomelanosis of Ito is the hypopigmented counterpart

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Mosaic pigmentary disorders). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
